hypothesis: Exact registered writer; one complete source word per complete observed working-unit group; fixed bijective17consonant/5vowel mapping; no hidden END, clipping, omissions or postword decoration.
implication: Every source word ending with a consonant C produces an output group whose final two COMPLETE working units are equal to key(C).
proof: At sourcewordend a consonant has no following vowel. The mandatory encoder otherwise-branch emits key(C),key(C).
No subsequent source token is present, so those two units are exactly the output tail. The key is bijective but its value is irrelevant to equality.

Consequently the number of consonant-final source words is at most the number of corresponding output groups with equal final units. One-unit output groups cannot be consonant-final under this writer.

converse_counterexample.conclusion: A doubled native ending does not establish a source coda or assign any native sound.

population_condition: For a frozen population of N complete emitted words, CODA_COUNT<=FINAL_DOUBLE_COUNT and CODA_SHARE<=FINAL_DOUBLE_COUNT/N. Do not replace the matching population with another sample or call an excluded/uncertain group non-double. Report exact eligible denominator and every exclusion.
optional_tighter_bound: If all22native units are fixed and counted, actual coda-double tails use only the17unit images of consonants. Maximizing the sum of final-double counts over17units would sharpen a necessary ceiling. The unconditional bound requires no such optimization; no source alphabet or key is selected.
interpretation: A low ceiling would impose a source coda-frequency obligation, not refute this arbitrary-source family or every human language. To reject a particular source hypothesis its tokenization/normalization and whole-word correspondence must be independently fixed.
